title: The India–US trade deal
summary:
India and the United States began work on a Bilateral Trade Agreement in February 2025. The goal was to more than double two-way trade to 500 billion dollars by 2030. Talks soon ran into trouble. By late August 2025, American tariffs on most Indian goods had climbed to 50 percent, including a penalty over India's purchases of Russian oil.

In February 2026, the two sides agreed a framework for a first, interim deal. Washington cut its tariff on Indian goods to 18 percent and dropped the oil penalty. Weeks later, the US Supreme Court struck down the tariffs that the deal was built around. That sent negotiators back to the table. In October 2026, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the first part of the trade deal was finalised and in legal drafting. On 20 October, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in Mumbai that the two sides were very, very close.
watch: Marco Rubio's India visit runs until 22 October, with a stop at the Jamnagar refinery. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer has said President Trump and Prime Minister Modi may speak again soon. The open questions are a signing date, the final tariff rate India gets compared with rivals like Vietnam, access for American dairy, the outcome of US trade investigations, and India's Russian oil purchases. US midterm elections fall on 3 November.

timeline.title: Modi and Trump launch the trade talks
timeline.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met President Donald Trump in Washington. The two leaders launched a plan called Mission 500, to more than double two-way trade to 500 billion dollars by 2030. They agreed to negotiate the first part of a Bilateral Trade Agreement by the autumn of 2025.

sources.title: India, US eye trade deal by Oct as Trump vows reciprocal tariffs in talks with Modi

timeline.title: First round of talks held in New Delhi
timeline.text: Indian commerce officials and the office of the US Trade Representative met in New Delhi from 26 to 29 March. They agreed on next steps toward finishing the first part of the trade deal by autumn. Market access and cutting tariff and non-tariff barriers were among the priorities.

sources.title: India, US agree to finalise first tranche of bilateral trade agreement by fall 2025

timeline.title: Trump announces a 26 percent tariff on India
timeline.text: President Trump announced so-called reciprocal tariffs on dozens of countries. India was given a rate of 26 percent, which Trump called discounted. He said India charged the United States 52 percent on its goods. The rate was due to take effect on 9 April.

sources.title: United States imposes 26% reciprocal tariffs on India

timeline.title: A 25 percent tariff on India is announced
timeline.text: On 30 July, Trump announced a 25 percent tariff on Indian goods, plus an unspecified penalty. An executive order set the 25 percent rate to start on 7 August. At the time, a US team was still due in New Delhi on 25 August for the sixth round of talks.

sources.title: Trump penalises 70 nations; 25% levy on India from Aug 7

timeline.title: Russian oil penalty takes tariffs to 50 percent
timeline.text: On 6 August, Trump signed an order adding another 25 percent tariff on India over its imports of Russian oil. It took effect on 27 August, taking the total to 50 percent. The talks planned for 25 to 29 August were postponed.

sources.title: Trump imposes new 25% tariff on India for buying Russian oil, raising total to 50%
India, US resume trade talks in Delhi as US trade representative Bendan Lynch arrives

timeline.title: Talks resume in New Delhi
timeline.text: Assistant US Trade Representative Brendan Lynch came to New Delhi to restart the stalled talks. He met India's chief negotiator, Rajesh Agrawal. Progress had been slow, as India resisted American demands to open its farm and dairy sectors.

sources.title: India, US resume trade talks in Delhi as US trade representative Bendan Lynch arrives

timeline.title: Trump announces a deal and an 18 percent tariff
timeline.text: After a call with Prime Minister Modi, Trump announced a trade deal. He said the tariff on Indian goods would fall to 18 percent, and that India would stop buying Russian oil. A White House official said the 25 percent oil penalty would be dropped. Modi said he was delighted that Made in India products would now face a reduced tariff of 18 percent.

sources.title: US to cut tariffs on India to 18%, India agrees to end Russian oil purchases

timeline.title: Framework for an interim deal is agreed
timeline.text: The two countries issued a joint statement setting out a framework for an interim trade deal. India agreed to cut or remove tariffs on all American industrial goods and many farm products. It said it intends to buy 500 billion dollars of American energy, aircraft, technology and other goods over five years. Trump also signed an order ending the Russian oil penalty from 7 February.

sources.title: India, US Reach Framework For Interim Trade Agreement; PM Modi Hails It As 'Great News'
US drops 25 per cent tariff on Indian imports

timeline.title: US Supreme Court strikes down the tariffs
timeline.text: The US Supreme Court ruled that an emergency powers law did not let the president impose tariffs. That knocked out the tariffs used against India in 2025. The administration replaced them with a temporary global tariff that can last up to 150 days.

sources.title: Why US Supreme Court's Tariff Ruling Is Both Relief and Risk for India

timeline.title: New US probe covers India and signing is put off
timeline.text: On 11 March, the US Trade Representative opened investigations into India and 15 other economies over excess factory capacity, which could lead to new tariffs. Days later, an Indian official said the interim deal would be signed only after Washington settles its new tariff plans. The deal had been expected to be signed by mid March.

sources.title: US to probe 'unfair trade practices' by India, 15 other countries; inquiry may lead to new tariffs
India–US Interim Trade Deal Put on Hold Until New US Tariff Framework

timeline.title: Rubio says a deal is on the verge in New Delhi
timeline.text: Secretary of State Marco Rubio met External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi. Rubio said the two sides had made tremendous progress and were on the verge of a trade agreement. He gave no timeline.

sources.title: US, India on verge of trade deal, 'tremendous progress' in talks: Marco Rubio

timeline.title: Greer says a deal is not imminent
timeline.text: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said a deal with India was not imminent, though both sides had identified the sticking points. That came about a week after Piyush Goyal called the deal almost done and dusted. A few days later, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the talks had reached a plateau.

sources.title: Identified the items but India-US trade deal not imminent, says USTR Jamieson Greer
India-US trade deal's first tranche finalised, undergoing legal drafting and final review: Piyush Goyal

timeline.title: Goyal says first part is in legal drafting
timeline.text: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the first part of the trade deal had been finalised and was going through legal drafting. He said it would be put into effect once India gets a competitive edge over rival countries. The next day, Nirmala Sitharaman said she hoped the deal would be concluded soon.

sources.title: First tranche of India-US trade deal finalised, undergoing legal drafting, says Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal
India-US trade deal nears finish as Rubio heads to India

timeline.title: Rubio in Mumbai says the deal is very close
timeline.text: Marco Rubio held talks with S Jaishankar in Mumbai at the start of a three-day visit. Rubio said the two sides were very, very close, with a small number of items left to wrap up. India has said its final tariff rate should be similar to those of rivals such as Vietnam.

sources.title: Rubio and Jaishankar hold talks in Mumbai as US and India aim to finalize trade deal
Rubio begins India visit, to hold crucial talks with Jaishankar in Mumbai
